simple.meaning: קְלִיטָא (Qᵉlîyṭâʼ) is a Hebrew word meaning “Kelita , the name of three Israelites.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: קְלִיטָא (H7042) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Ezra 10:23, with occurrences in Ezra, Nehemiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קְלִיטָא (H7042) in the Hebrew text.

occurrences.englishText: Of the Levites: Jozabad, and Shimei, and Kelaiah (also called Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.

Also Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites, caused the people to understand the law; and the people stayed in their place.
